title: Good Days, Bad Days
subtitle: The era can shape us, but it can also destroy us. So just relax and take it easy, everyone says.

items.text: Meeting Room, Rayashki

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I don't see the point of your reluctance.
The frowning master of ceremonies straightens the tortoise-patterned letter and then shoves it back into its envelope.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: The letter conveyed Zeno's decision clearly.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I suggest we warm ourselves up with a few drinks before we go. Do you have any Stolich in town?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Better than sitting here dwelling on the things that cannot be changed.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Please tell me you have something like cocoa here.
Their long-awaited guest stretches lazily, as if no one is around, and sinks into the couch.
The tension in the air hangs like fumes waiting to ignite.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: This is not what we agreed on earlier, Mr. Bertolt.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Calm yourself, Vila.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You must be mistaken, my very passionate friend.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno sent a warning months ago. "The estimated value Rayashki can add to Zeno's program is less than satisfactory. Further support is no longer recommended."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: "Should any new valuable resources be found in the region, please reply to this letter as soon as possible for further assessment."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Then we heard back from Rayashki.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: In fact, the sender was you, Evgeni.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Yes, it was.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And it was you yourself that argued the most compelling point, I have to say. One that has drawn the higher-ups' attention, and the reason why I was sent here.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I believe you wrote: "I have total faith in the quality of the people of Rayashki. Their solidarity, dedication, and motivation have proven invaluable to us."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: "I am certain they would carry those same strengths of character and skill to any post, no matter where they were assigned."
He folds the letter and hands it to Vila, her face blank as a canvas.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Zeno accepted my application.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Of course, I asked around before making my submission, and Zeno seemed to have a good reputation.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: It was a golden opportunity to join them.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: It is, but do not get us wrong. Our entrance requirements can be most difficult to meet.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno only takes in the best of the best.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You want some of us to work for Zeno?!

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You never told us anything like that, Evgeni!

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Be reasonable, Vila. Some of us deserve this opportunity.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What about the others?! We have elders and children. Some of our comrades have been injured and even died in the mine; are we to forget their sacrifices?
She tries to suppress the gills on her neck as they heave violently.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Relax, my friend. That's why we sent our very best biological control squad.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We will escort you to the nearest shelter.
Another wave upon relentless waves of shock.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Face reality, Vila. I know how much effort we have put into building this town, and I understand you have this dream to fulfill.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But we must prepare for the worst: we may have to give up on our Rayashki.
He takes out a document covered in scratched notes and annotations and hands it to her.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: Read this.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Field investigation has confirmed that the remaining runium reserves in Rayashki are around 0.0173 kilotons, which is less than 0.275% of our average annual output."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "The mine is located high within the Arctic Circle, which has entailed significant transportation costs. The harsh environment is also wholly unsuitable for building any permanent processing facilities."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "In addition, military spending on the region has recently been elevated 3.61 times due to increasing animal and critter attacks, and that number is still rising."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Clearly, the region is now incapable of self-management."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "According to the Guide on Global Humanitarian Aid by the Office for Disaster Risk Reduction of Zeno Arms Academy, we propose to ..."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "... send a special squad to the region to evacuate all local citizens and subsequently take care of the remaining biological control issues."

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And our admission standards will be lowered—at Zeno's discretion—so that you will all find work with us somewhere.
Zeno's representative offers a timely, if unconvincing, supplement to the letter.
The paper creases and crumples into a ball in her hands.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I'm sorry, but this is reality.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: From the start, this ore was the only thing they wanted from us.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: The environment here has always been harsh for mining, but we overcame it and sent our shipments to wherever Zeno had need of them.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And I salute each one of you for your work, my friends.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: But now, our mission is over.
There is no doubt in anyone's mind: runium has been the town's lifeblood and the key to its survival.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I believe all of you will continue to work hard in your new positions. No matter what ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You shouldn't rush to a decision. We're discussing Rayashki's future here, Evgeni.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: For six decades, the people here have put in great efforts to turn the town into what it is today. We won't leave just because you tell us so.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Our grandparents didn't even have construction equipment at the beginning. They built these houses with their own hands.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: We shipped over the planting soil. We built walls to keep out the wind and snow.
Within the meeting room's cloistered walls, the air is heavy with moisture once more.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: When you came here, you brought books for the children and introduced us to a species different than humans. You became one of us.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I am not happy about this either, Comrade Vila.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I won't buy that, Comrade Evgeni. This is not just about my dream, but everyone's dream.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Or have you forgotten what Rayashki was meant to be?

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: A utopia built for and by everyone. The voice of a better future, one which would sound across the land and seas.

items.speaker: Evgeni
items.text: I remember every word of it.
Evgeni's voice is low but still decisive.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: You have my sympathy, friends.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Zeno has also suffered huge losses in many regions.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We have lost manpower, territory, armament factories, and even some of our affiliated military schools. Rayashki is but one of these losses.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We know how you feel right now.
He shrugs his shoulders, his face a picture of unhelpfulness.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: But Zeno has its own problems to be faced.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: And investing in these new industries, purchasing fancy equipment, all these things Rayashki will need ... All of this takes money. And even Zeno must be economical.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Shouldn't the people in Rayashki also benefit from these global benefits Zeno has promised?

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We will get there, my friend. Maybe slowly, but we will get there. Trust me, Zeno has done everything they can for you.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: We need to keep our eyes on our goals and stay on the right course, so that we won't get lost in these turbulent times, yes?
He leans toward Vila, providing an unnecessary whisper.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: I know how much faith these people have in you, and I believe you can show them a different perspective about these coming changes.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Of course, this will also help you during Zeno's assessment.

items.speaker: Bertolt
items.text: Good luck, my friend.
